How to do itChin-up

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Bar just below the finger base, thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Wrong: Wrist curled forward, so the grip is weaker.

Shoulder set

Seen from behind
Right
SHOULDERS DOWN
Wrong
SHRUGGED

Right: Shoulder blades down and back before the arms bend.

Wrong: Shoulders shrugged to the ears at the start.

Body line

Right
BODY VERTICAL
Wrong
LEGS KICK

Right: Legs crossed and still, body vertical under the bar.

Wrong: Legs kicking forward to throw the chin up.

Pull the shoulder blades down and back before the arms bend, and hold them there.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Legs kickThe legs kick forward to swing the body up.
  2. Body arcsThe body arcs back to throw the chin over the bar.
Pull2 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Palms facing you, bar just below the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped.

Keep your wrist straight, in line with your forearm, not curled.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging or kicking up

    Fix: Cross your legs, brace and keep your body vertical.

  • Half reps

    Fix: Straight arms at the bottom, chin to the bar every rep.

  • Shoulders up at the start

    Fix: Pull your shoulders down and back, then bend your arms.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your back and your biceps.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou start the pull with your shoulders up by your ears.

    FixSet your shoulders down and back before each rep.

  • Usually meansArms high overhead narrow the space under the shoulder roof.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

  • Usually meansToo much pulling volume, too soon.

    FixAdd sets slowly. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Palms facing you, full grip, thumbs wrapped round the bar.

  2. 2

    Hands about shoulder-width apart, or slightly closer.

  3. 3

    Hang, cross one leg over the other and brace your abs.

  4. 4

    Pull your shoulders down and back before you bend your arms.

  5. 5

    Can't do a full rep yet? Use band or machine help.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arms high overhead narrow the space under the shoulder roof.
  • Of the pulls tested, chin-ups and pull-ups loaded the spine most.
  • Elbows can get overused when pulling volume rises too fast.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

Elbow pain

Severe pain and hard to move, heard a snap, changed shape, tingling, or numbness? Get it checked today.

How to do itHanging Knee Raise

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Base of fingers

Wrong: Wrist curled

Top position

Right
KNEES ABOVE HIPS
Wrong
STOPPED AT HIPS

Right: Knees above hip height, pelvis curled up.

Wrong: Knees stopped at hip height, pelvis not curled.

Body line

Right
BODY STILL
Wrong
BODY SWINGS

Right: Body still under the bar on every rep.

Wrong: Body swinging to kick the legs up.

Start every rep from a still hang, with no swing.

  1. Body swingsThe body swings to help the legs up.
  2. Legs kicked upThe swing kicks the knees up, not the abs.
Lift1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, bar just below the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped. Arms fully straight.

Keep your wrist from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging the body

    Fix: Start each rep from a still hang. Lower with control.

  • Knees stop at hip height

    Fix: Lift past hip height and roll your hips up.

  • Dropping the legs fast

    Fix: Lower the legs with control.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your belly and the front of your hips.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansKnees stop near hip height, so the hip flexors do the lifting.

    FixLift the knees higher and curl the pelvis up at the top.

  • FixUse arm straps (ab slings).

  • Usually meansStraight legs load the spine more, bent knees likely less.

    FixKeep the knees bent.

  • Usually meansArms high overhead narrow the space under the shoulder roof.

    FixPull your shoulder blades down and back. If it hurts, stop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Use a bar high enough that you hang with straight legs.

  2. 2

    Take the bar overhand, hands shoulder width, thumbs wrapped.

  3. 3

    Hang with straight arms and let your body go still.

  4. 4

    Pull your shoulder blades down and back as you hang.

  5. 5

    New to it? Keep the knees bent until this is easy.

Risks and when to stop

  • Straight legs load the spine more, bent knees likely less.
  • A long hang with arms overhead narrows the space under the shoulder roof.

How to do itAssisted Pull-up

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Overhand, thumb wrapped, wrist not curled.

Wrong: Wrist curled

Bottom position

Right
ARMS STRAIGHT
Wrong

Right: Both knees on the pad, arms fully straight.

Wrong: Arms still bent at the bottom: a half rep.

Shoulder set

Seen from behind
Right
SHOULDERS DOWN
Wrong
SHRUGGED

Right: Shoulder blades down and back at the start.

Wrong: Shoulders shrugged up to the ears.

Kneel on the pad and let it sink until the arms are straight.

Tells
  1. Arms bentThe arms never straighten at the bottom: a half rep.
  2. Pad stays upThe pad never sinks to the dead hang.
Lower3 s
Pull2 s
Hold1 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs wrapped around the bar.

Keep your wrist from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Dropping fast when lowering

    Fix: Take three to four seconds to lower to straight arms.

  • Stopping short

    Fix: Full hang to chin over the bar. Can't? Add a little assistance.

  • Swinging or leg drive

    Fix: Add assistance until every rep is controlled.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your back and your arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou start the pull with your shoulders up by your ears.

    FixDraw your shoulders down and back first, then bend your arms.

  • Usually meansArms high overhead narrow the space under the shoulder roof.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

  • Usually meansToo much pulling volume, too soon.

    FixAdd sets slowly. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    More stack weight, more help. Use the least for full reps.

  2. 2

    Overhand, about shoulder width or a little wider, thumbs wrapped.

  3. 3

    Knees securely on the pad. Let it sink until your arms straighten.

  4. 4

    Blades down and back, then pull elbows to ribs, chest up.

  5. 5

    Over the weeks, add reps first, then take assistance away.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arms overhead narrow the space under the shoulder roof.
  • Elbows can get overused when pulling volume rises too fast.
  • Resting your chin or neck on the pad loads the neck.

How to do itInverted Row

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Overhand, thumb wrapped, wrist not curled.

Wrong: Wrist curled

Body line

Right
BODY STRAIGHT
Wrong
HIPS SAG

Right: Heels, hips and shoulders in one straight line.

Wrong: Hips sagging toward the floor.

Top position

Right
CHEST TO BAR
Wrong
SHORT OF BAR

Right: Chest touching the bar, shoulder blades squeezed back.

Wrong: Chest well short of the bar.

Keep a rigid straight line from head to heels, top and bottom.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips saggingThe hips drop toward the floor and the body folds.
Pull1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, bar across the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped.

Keep your wrist from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Hips sagging

    Fix: Keep your whole body rigid. Can't? Raise the bar.

  • Stopping short of the bar

    Fix: Pull until your chest touches the bar.

  • Dropping back down fast

    Fix: Lower yourself with control to straight arms.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between your shoulder blades and down the sides of your back.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe trunk is working hard to hold the line.

    FixKeep the body rigid. Raise the bar if the line breaks.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set a bar in a rack at about waist height.

  2. 2

    Overhand, slightly wider than your shoulders, thumbs wrapped.

  3. 3

    Hang under it, body straight from head to heels.

  4. 4

    Pull your shoulder blades back and down as you row.

  5. 5

    Too hard? Raise the bar. Too easy? Feet on a box.

Risks and when to stop

  • Stiff shoulders or arms? Rings let them move more freely than a bar.

How to do itClose-Grip Pulldown

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Neutral grip on the V-handle, wrists not curled.

Wrong: Wrist curled

Bottom position

Right
ELBOWS TO HIPS
Wrong
ELBOWS BEHIND

Right: Handle just below the chin, upper arms tucked.

Wrong: Handle past the chin, elbows moving back.

Knee pad: right and wrong

Right
PAD ON THIGHS
Wrong
PAD TOO HIGH

Right: Pad firm on the thighs, hips down.

Wrong: Pad too high, hips lifting.

Set the thigh pad tight on top of the thighs.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Pulled too lowThe handle is pulled past the chin, down the chest.
  2. Elbows behindThe elbows drive back behind the body.
Pull2 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

V-handle, palms facing each other, thumbs around the handle.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pulling too low

    Fix: Stop when the handle is just below your chin.

  • Rocking the torso back

    Fix: Hold a slight lean and keep it still.

  • Fast return

    Fix: Control the handle all the way back up.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your lats, along the sides of your back.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are pulling too low.

    FixStop just below the chin, when the elbows stop moving down.

  • Usually meansThe handle is going too low.

    FixStop just below the chin.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Clip a V-handle to the cable.

  2. 2

    Set the thigh pads tight on your thighs when you sit.

  3. 3

    Palms facing each other, thumbs around the handle.

  4. 4

    Lean back slightly, no more than about 30 degrees.

  5. 5

    Draw your shoulder blades down to start the pull.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pulling past where the elbows stop moving down stresses the shoulder.

Hand: right and wrong

Wrong: Wrist curled

Torso lean

Right
SLIGHT LEAN

Grip

Underhand, palms facing you. Thumbs wrapped or thumbless, either is fine.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pulling too far

    Fix: Stop when the bar passes just below your chin.

  • Rocking the torso

    Fix: Keep the torso still.

  • Bar flying back up

    Fix: Control it all the way up. Can't? Go lighter.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your lats. Pull your elbows back and down toward your glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are pulling the bar too low.

    FixStop just below the chin.

  • Usually meansThe grip is too wide, or you pull too far.

    FixBring the hands in to shoulder width. Stop when the elbows stop moving down.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Sit and set the pads tight against your thighs.

  2. 2

    Stand, take the bar underhand about shoulder width, then sit.

  3. 3

    Lean back slightly, no more than about 30 degrees.

  4. 4

    Draw your shoulder blades down to start the pull.

  5. 5

    Can't control the bar on the way up? Go lighter.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pulling past where the elbows stop moving down stresses the shoulder.

How to do itSingle-Arm Lat Pulldown

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Single handle, wrist not curled.

Wrong: Wrist curled

Bottom position

Right
ARM AT SIDE
Wrong
ELBOW BEHIND

Right: Upper arm flush with the side, shoulder down.

Wrong: Elbow behind the body, shoulder rolled forward.

  1. Elbow goes backThe elbow drives back behind the body past the end.
  2. Pulled too lowThe handle keeps going down well past the chin.
Pull2 s
Hold1 s

Grip

Single handle, thumb around it.

Keep the wrist from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pulling past the end

    Fix: Stop when the handle just passes your chin.

  • Twisting the torso

    Fix: Brace the trunk. Still twisting? Lower the load.

  • Leaning into each rep

    Fix: Tighten your abs to hold the spine still.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your lat. The side of your waist works to stop you twisting.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou pull past the end and the shoulder rolls forward.

    FixStop when the handle passes your chin.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Clip a single handle to the cable.

  2. 2

    Stand to take the handle, then sit, thighs tight under the pads.

  3. 3

    Use less than half your two-arm pulldown weight to start.

  4. 4

    Brace your trunk so it won't twist.

  5. 5

    No pulldown machine? Kneel at a cable machine.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rolling the shoulder forward at the end of the pull may stress it.

How to do itStraight-Arm Pulldown

Elbow bend

Right
SLIGHT BEND
Wrong
ELBOWS BEND

Right: Arm almost straight, same slight bend all rep.

Wrong: Elbow bent at the bottom, like a pushdown.

Trunk position

Right
CHEST TALL
Wrong
BACK ARCHED

Right: Trunk braced and still, chest tall at the bottom.

Wrong: Lower back arched.

Keep the same slight elbow bend from top to bottom. Only the shoulders move.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows bendThe elbows bend and the lift turns into a pushdown.
  2. Bar pulled inThe elbows bend as the bar comes down, turning it into a bent-arm pulldown.
Pull2 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand on a straight bar, hands about shoulder width or a little wider.

Common handling mistakes

  • Bending the elbows

    Fix: Keep the same slight elbow bend all set.

  • Too much weight

    Fix: Lower the weight until you can pause at the bottom.

  • Arching the lower back

    Fix: Brace the stomach and move only the arms.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your lats, with little biceps or upper-back work.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWatch for an arching lower back or a swinging torso.

    FixBrace and move only the arms.

  • Usually meansWatch for bending elbows, which turns it into a pushdown.

    FixKeep the same slight elbow bend top to bottom.

  • Usually meansGoing too heavy brings jerking, torso swing and momentum.

    FixDrop the weight until you can pause at the bottom.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pulley at its highest point and attach a straight bar.

  2. 2

    Take the bar overhand, hands about shoulder width or a little wider.

  3. 3

    Step back until the cable is taut. Feet hip width, knees soft.

  4. 4

    Chest up, trunk braced, at most a slight lean forward.

  5. 5

    Pick a weight you can move smoothly, with a one-second squeeze.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching the lower back under the cable moves stress onto the lumbar spine.
  • Jerking a load that is too heavy swings the torso.

Chest on pad

Right
CHEST ON PAD
Wrong
LEANING BACK

Right: Chest lightly on the pad, trunk upright.

Wrong: Chest off the pad, trunk leaning back, lower back arched.

Right
JUST BEHIND YOU

Pull2 s

Look closer

Grip

Take the handles with straight arms. Keep your wrists in line with your forearms.

Keep your wrists in line with your forearms all set.

Common handling mistakes

  • Leaning back off the pad

    Fix: Keep your chest on the pad. Do not lean back.

  • Shoulders rounding forward

    Fix: Return slowly. Stop when your arms are straight, shoulders still back.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the middle of your back, between your shoulder blades.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWatch for leaning back off the pad and arching your lower back.

    FixKeep your chest on the pad. Do not lean back.

  • Usually meansWatch for your shoulder blades rounding forward on the return.

    FixReturn slowly and keep your shoulders back.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so the handles sit about level with your shoulders.

  2. 2

    Plant your feet on the floor or the foot pads.

  3. 3

    Set the chest pad to touch your chest lightly, arms straight.

  4. 4

    Sit tall, shoulders back and down, wrists straight.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Leaning back and arching adds needless stress to your lower back.
  • A free-weight row measured more lower-back muscle work than a machine row.

How to do itResistance Band Row

Back line

Right
SIT TALL
Wrong
BACK ROUNDS

Right: Sitting tall, back straight, holding the pull.

Wrong: Lower back rounded, trunk tipped forward.

Shoulder blades

Seen from behind
Right
SQUEEZED

Right: Shoulder blades squeezed together at the end.

Wrong: Shoulder blades still apart at the end of the pull.

Back straight and neutral, chest up, the same from start to finish.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Low back roundsThe lower back rounds and the trunk tips forward.
  2. Trunk tips forwardThe trunk tips forward over the legs instead of staying tall.
Pull2 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

Band flat in your palm, long end round the back of your hand. Grip it firmly.

Keep your wrists straight, in line with your forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Letting the band snap back

    Fix: Control the way back to the start.

  • Slumping while holding the band

    Fix: Sit tall first. If you can't, hold the band further along.

  • A worn or loose band

    Fix: Check the band each session. Anchor it firmly round your soles.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this as a small squeeze between your shoulder blades.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWatch for losing your tall, straight back.

    FixSit tall. Hold the band further along so it stretches less.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Check the band for wear. Breathe out as you pull.

  2. 2

    Sit on a mat, legs straight out, feet flexed.

  3. 3

    Loop the band round both soles. Wrap an end round each hand.

  4. 4

    Hold the band shorter or longer to change how hard it is.

  5. 5

    Sit tall, shoulders down and back, arms straight in front.

Risks and when to stop

  • A worn or loosely anchored band can snap back.
  • Avoid holding the pull with your lower back rounded.

How to do itIncline Machine Press

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Heel of your palm, thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Wrong: Handle in your fingers, wrist bent back, thumb loose.

Push through the heel of your palm, wrist in line with your forearm. Thumbs wrapped round the handles.

Shoulder blades

Right
BLADES ON PAD
Wrong
BLADES OFF PAD

Right: Blades flat on the pad, hands at forehead height.

Wrong: Upper back rounded forward off the pad.

At the start the hands sit level with the upper chest or shoulders.

Tells
  1. Blades off padThe shoulder blades round forward off the pad at the top of the press.
  2. Rolls forwardThe shoulders roll forward, so the arms reach past the end of the press.
Press2 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s

Also check your wrist:

Look closer

Grip

Push through the heel of your palm, wrist in line with your forearm. Thumbs wrapped round the handles.

Keep your wrist in line with your forearm.

Common handling mistakes

  • Blades rolling off the pad

    Fix: Stop the press with the blades still on the pad.

  • Arching the lower back

    Fix: Brace and keep only the natural low-back curve.

  • Snapping the elbows locked

    Fix: Stop just before the elbows lock, pause, then lower slowly.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your upper chest.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWatch for your shoulder blades rolling off the pad at the top.

    FixKeep the blades on the pad and stop the press there.

  • Usually meansWatch for your lower back arching off the pad.

    FixBrace and keep only the natural low-back curve.

  • Usually meansWatch for locking your elbows at the top.

    FixStop just short of lockout.

  • Usually meansWatch for the wrist bending out of line with the forearm.

    FixKeep the wrist in line with the forearm.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so your hands start level with your upper chest.

  2. 2

    Sit back against the pad, feet planted.

  3. 3

    Handle in the heel of your palm, wrist straight.

  4. 4

    Brace, keep the natural low-back curve, shoulders back and down.

  5. 5

    One or two reps over target? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Blades rolling off the pad leave the shoulder blades less stable.
  • Arching the lower back off the pad is a fault to avoid.

Common handling mistakes

  • Letting the handles drop

    Fix: Stop just before the elbows lock, pause, then lower.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the fronts and sides of your shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWatch for letting the handles drop on the way down.

    FixStop the set.

  • Usually meansWatch for the low back arching off the pad.

    FixBrace, keep the natural curve, and lower the weight.

  • Usually meansYour elbows lock at the top.

    FixStop just short of lockout.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat: handles at or just above shoulder height.

  2. 2

    Sit back against the pad, feet planted. Breathe out as you press.

  3. 3

    Full grip, thumbs round, wrists straight.

  4. 4

    Brace, keep the natural low-back curve, shoulders back and down.

  5. 5

    One or two reps over target? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • The shoulder is less stable overhead. Never let the handles drop.
  • Arching the low back off the pad to finish reps.
  • Very heavy lifts with breath holding sent blood pressure very high.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

Back pain

Pain, numbness, tingling or weakness in both legs? Numb genitals or anus? Bladder, bowel or sexual changes? Chest pain? Serious accident? Get emergency help now. Sudden severe or fast-worsening pain? Hot, cold, shivery or unwell? See a doctor today.

No better in a few weeks? See a doctor.

Elbow pain

Severe pain and hard to move, heard a snap, changed shape, tingling, or numbness? Get it checked today.

No better after a few weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.
